title: Beyond Caption-Based Queries for Video Moment Retrieval

problems.name: Multi-Moment, Compositional, and Complex Query Grounding
problems.evidence_sentence: We iden- 1 arXiv:2603.02363v1 [cs.CV] 2 Mar 2026 --- Page 2 --tify two key factors driving this degradation: (i) a language gap, reflecting the linguistic distribution shift between caption and search queries, and (ii) a multi-moment gap, arising from how caption-based queries map to a single ground-truth (GT) moment, while the under-specified search queries often map to multiple moments.

problems.name: Domain Shift and Generalization
problems.evidence_sentence: Our analysis reveals two key generalization challenges: (i) A language gap, arising from the linguistic under-specification of search queries, and (ii) a multi-moment gap, caused by the shift from single-moment to multi-moment queries.

problems.name: Dataset, Benchmark, and Evaluation Mismatch
problems.evidence_sentence: The code, models and data are available in the project webpage: https://davidpujol.github.io/beyond-vmr/ # Abstract In this work, we investigate the degradation of existing VMR methods, particularly of DETR architectures, when trained on caption-based queries but evaluated on search queries.

methods.name: Transformer/DETR-Style Proposal Decoding
methods.evidence_sentence: DETR [6] has become the cornerstone of most existing VMR methods [17, 29, 38, 50], thanks to its usage of K learnable decoder queries, each of which maps to a potential retrieved moment with a corresponding confidence score.
